summary.intent: Merge origin/main (which now includes #246) into the #242 branch, resolving conflicts in init.rs, init/tests.rs and add.rs while keeping both sides' behaviour. Then add combined init acceptance tests, run the full gate and a targeted Codex review, and report the sha without pushing.
summary.outcome: The merge conflicts were resolved with both sides kept, lib tests pass (238), the combined workflow-outcome matrix test passes, and the merge was committed with a signed commit. The full gate and the targeted Codex review have not run yet, and the final sha was not reported in the transcript.

repo: The repo's lint rejects eprintln!/println! in callisto-cli and callisto-graph. Prompt text must go through crate::output::prompt_line (fallible, returns io::Result) and advisory messages through advise(&mut stderr, ...) (best effort).
#246's tty.rs printed prompt text with eprintln!/eprint!. The merge converted required prompt text to prompt_line(..)? and made print_list return io::Result<()>.

#246 replaced the bool `interactive` parameter with Option<tty::Prompts> (capability: Text + TTY stdin + TTY stderr; JSON never prompts). Under #242, run/run_queued take `prompts`, and tests pass Some(Prompts::for_tests()) or None.
#242 emits notes (e.g. existing-workflow skip, missing origin remote) as queued diagnostics on stderr exactly once. #246 tests that expected those on stdout had to be updated to check stderr once.

#242's JSON-mode decline test no longer applies because JSON never prompts under #246. It was rewritten as a Text-mode decline test asserting one note on stderr, one tty::CANCELLED on stdout, and no callisto.toml or .changeset/README.md written.

The workflow classification: only GraphError::InitWorkflowExists skips the question with a 'Keeping the existing ... workflow' note. Other automatic failures warn with 'Skipping the GitHub Actions workflow: ...' and continue.

code.finding: Added `use crate::output::prompt_line;` and made list/prompt helpers fallible so prompt output errors propagate instead of being swallowed by eprintln!.
Took #246's wizard wholesale, then rewired it to use fallible prompt_line(..)? for required output and advise() for the 'Next:' hint and warnings.

Kept #242's Notes/advise_diagnostics and exactly-once lifecycle with #246's prompts capability and workflow classification. The `interactive` parameter was renamed to `prompts: Option<tty::Prompts>` in run and run_queued.

workflow: The peer lead asks for a targeted `codex exec` review against the #242 contract, the handoff's Workstream2 and the 'Combined acceptance cases' rather than bare `codex review --base origin/main`, which missed real defects. The review should check siblings and write throwaway failing tests, and only confirmed failures should be reported.
Loop: fix confirmed defects, re-gate, and repeat until Codex confirms none. Then report the sha and do not push.
The Python `str.replace` with `assert a in s` pattern worked well for scripted conflict resolution because it fails loudly when the expected text is absent.
Merge-base was found by sha (39a70f311) to diff the base, #242 and main versions of init.rs and see what each side changed.

friction: The first `git merge` command's grep pipeline was re-run via `rtk grep`, suggesting the first attempt failed or produced no usable output.
Shell quoting in the inline python edit scripts was fragile, with \\n escapes inside nested quotes.
The conflict markers in init.rs needed several rounds of manual cleanup, with a few Edit calls and re-greps.
The first attempt to diff base vs main init.rs failed because merge-base was not resolved, so it had to be redone with explicit shas.
An in-flight gate on the stale sha 3e902a31b had to be stopped and its work discarded when #246 merged.

Report the final sha to the lead session without pushing.
